newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Maori groups meet over forestry claims.
newsitem.headline: Maori groups meet over forestry claims.

text.p: Te Arawa Mataatua Forest Accord was to meet central North Island forestry land claimants on Monday to discuss whether they should join forces in a $400 million mass land claim, the New Zealand Press Association reported.
Those at the meeting in Rotorua would also discuss whether the land claims should be settled under the Crown Forests Assets Act, accord convener Leith Comer said.
Under the Act, successful claimants would get their land back, a minimum of 5 percent of the value of the trees and accrued rental which added up to $400 million.
Some tribes and sub tribes had reservations about a mass land claim. However, Comer said a single claim could speed up the settlement process.
The Waitangi Tribunal had shown in the past it required all the Maori issues to be sorted out beforehand. There were multiple claims and other tribal issues still to be resolved.
"If we put that to one side and focus on the issue of greater importance, which is between Maori and the Crown, we could get the land returned earlier than if we did things individually," Comer said.
With the Crown having already sold cutting rights in the forests to Fletcher Challenge, it was not clear whether it wanted to remain "landlord" for ever, Comer said.

The return of the land would also create economic opportunities. "We are hoping we can come up with the process that sorts out Maori issues. If we can get our land back we can become proper members of the forestry industry."
